judged_text: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is defined as `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, so its runtime value is the raw AES-256 encryption key string (or empty string), not a boolean. Any log line, error report, or serialized config that includes this exported flag prints the key that decrypts every synced app credential, and consumers that compare === true or persist the value get the secret itself instead of an on/off flag.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `export const APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED = process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY;` in `packages/lib/constants.ts`. In JS/TS, `a && b` returns `b` when `a` is truthy, so when both env vars are set this exported value becomes the raw `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` string (and can also become the raw webhook secret when the second operand is falsy), not a boolean. This is a security/correctness defect for an exported flag: any code that serializes/prints/compares the flag as a boolean could inadvertently propagate the secret value, and the name strongly implies it should be `true|false`.
